maya: Quick heads-up — after pushing kernel-selector v1.14 we started seeing p99 regressions for mixtral-moex in us-west. Rough pattern: 10-25% higher p99 for sequences above ~512 tokens, sustained across several hosts. Suspect interplay between kernel choice (parallel-topk), our soft-latency batcher, and KV cache hotset behavior.

sam: Which exact model variant, and can you paste a short profiler excerpt? Region/pool?

maya: Variant: mixtral-11b-moex (rope_scale=1.0, kv_dim=64, heads=32). Canary in us-west-a/b. Short profile snippet: 
``nrouter_eval p99: 120ms -> 270ms
kv_lookup p99: 18ms -> 140ms
kernel_choice: selected parallel-topk v2 (ROCm), heavy memcpy observed
batching: avg_batch_size fell from 28 -> 9 under soft-latency policy
```

liam: That aligns with the selector switching to parallel-topk because of sequence-length distribution shift. Parallel-topk does per-expert memcpy/gather; if router skew is high we'll repeatedly hit the same experts and thrash the KV cache.

rachel: We have seen similar when expert_parallelism was increased; eviction/load cycles dominated latency.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: deploy 1102 rolled to us-west at 2026-03-16T22:12Z (kernel/selector v1.13 -> v1.14)

sam: Hypothesis: router logits entropy dropped, so top-k keeps selecting a narrow set of experts; combined with smaller batches this prevents coalesced KV lookups and amplifies memcpy overheads.

maya: Repro command I used:
``nperf/loadtest --model mixtral-11b --mode seq --seq 1024 --qps 80 --batch-policy soft-latency --duration 10m
```
Quick stack break: 
``n[0.23s] expert_dispatch memcpy 45ms
[0.74s] kv_cache_load miss 120ms
[0.91s] kernel_wait memcpy 60ms
```

liam: Immediate mitigations to try:
  1) force selector to legacy topk path: REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREF=legacy_topk for moex
  2) increase batching window (e.g., 20ms) to allow larger coalesced batches
  3) reduce expert_parallelism temporarily to lower per-expert thread contention

maya: Applied mitigation (1) in canary (us-west-a) — p99 returned to baseline in ~30m. Strong signal this is selector + KV hotset interaction.

sam: Great. File a selector PR to make it conservative for moex and open a perf incident with dashboards and baseline screenshots.

maya: PR plan: have the selector prefer legacy_topk when (seq_len > 256) AND (moe.kv_hotset_eviction_rate > 0.2) OR router_logits_entropy < 1.2. I'll open PR + test matrix.

maya: Creating incident thread (triage) ts=2178888922

rachel: Longer-term fixes to explore:
  - Router: add soft-jitter/randomization to top-k selection when logits entropy is low to increase expert fanout
  - Kernel: implement fused/batched KV gather to collapse per-expert memcpy into a single fused kernel
  - Runtime metrics: publish moe.router_logits_entropy, moe.kv_hotset_eviction_rate, moe.per_expert_miss_rate for alerts and selector signals

dev-bot: noted. Owners assigned: @liam -> selector PR, @maya -> incident and canary validation, @rachel -> design doc for jittered-topk. Reminders scheduled.

liam: I'll draft the PR today with rollback tests and perf regressions attached. Draft link: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4182 (wip). Will add opt-in flag MOE_LEGACY_TOPK_FOR_HIGH_SEQ and a tunable selector threshold.

maya: Leaving canary pinned to legacy_topk until the selector PR is validated across regions. Adding entropy alert: moe.router_logits_entropy < 1.25 for 5m. Also adding a kv_eviction alert.

sam: Follow-ups: 1) long soak with mixed seq lengths and higher concurrency, 2) synthetic skewed-router sims to validate jittering, 3) grab flamegraphs for memcpy hotspots and KV load paths.

rachel: Also include RoPE scale sweep in the perf matrix — earlier experiments showed rope_scale deviations change logits distribution a bit, which could affect skew. Sweep values: 0.95, 1.0, 1.05; also vary heads/kv_dim.

maya: Will add those sweeps and update the incident. Plan to close after 48h stable canary.

sam: Thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:
